instructions: Answer any three out of the remaining five questions.
Assume any suitable data wherever required and justify the same.

questions.label: 1a
questions.text: Explain CAP. How is CAP different from ACID property in databases?

questions.label: 1b
questions.text: Secondary Name node is a backup of Name node. Is this statement True or False? Justify your answer.

questions.label: 1c
questions.text: List and explain the core business drivers behind the NoSQL movement.

questions.label: 1d
questions.text: List down any five constraints that must be satisfied for representing a stream by buckets using DGIM algorithm with examples.

questions.label: 2a
questions.text: List the architectural patterns in NoSQL databases. Discuss the Key-Value and Document-Oriented patterns, focusing on their characteristics, use cases, and examples.

questions.label: 2b
questions.text:
Write a map reduce pseudo code for word count problem. Apply map reduce working on the following document:

"This is NoSQL. NoSQL handles complex data."

questions.label: 3a
questions.text: Explain Map Reduce execution pipeline with suitable example.

questions.label: 3b
questions.text:
Create a Bloom filter with the following parameters:

Size of the bit array m = 8

Hash functions: h1(x) = x mod m, h2(x) = (2x + 1) mod m, h3(x) = (3x + 2) mod m

(i) Insert the following elements into the Bloom filter: 12, 25, 30, 5

(ii) Check if the following elements are present in the Bloom filter: 6, 55

(iii) Discuss the results of your checks, identifying which elements is true positive and which is true negative.

questions.label: 4a
questions.text: For the stream of integers: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Use the hash function, h(x) = (2x + 1) mod 32 and treat the result as a 5-bit binary integer. Show the steps of the Flajolet-Martin algorithm to estimate the number of distinct elements in this stream.

questions.label: 4b
questions.text: Draw a diagram of the typical Hadoop Ecosystem and explain any two components of it.

questions.label: 5a
questions.text: Write an algorithm for the Clique Percolation Method and discover the communities in the given below graph using Clique Percolation Method with clique k=3.
questions.note: Graph in the paper has 8 unlabelled nodes. Reading them as P1, P2, P3 (top row, left to right), Q1, Q2, Q3 (middle row) and R2, R3 (bottom row, under Q2 and Q3), the edges are: P1-P2, P2-P3, P1-Q1, P2-Q1, P2-Q2, P3-Q3, Q1-Q2, Q2-Q3, Q2-R2, Q2-R3, Q3-R2, Q3-R3, R2-R3.

questions.label: 5b
questions.text:
i. List and explain the functions provided by R to combine different sets of data.

ii. Write the script to sort the values contained in the following vector in ascending order and descending order: (46, 23, 15, 38, 98, 56, 28, 78). Demonstrate the output.

questions.label: 6a
questions.text:
The project manager at ABC Corp, Mr. Thomas, needs to track information about ongoing projects in the organization. He has the following details about current projects in a table format:

| ProjectId | ProjectName | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Website Redesign | 150000 |
| 2 | Mobile App Launch | 100000 |
| 3 | Data Migration | 80000 |
| 4 | AI Development | 200000 |
| 5 | Cybersecurity Audit | 50000 |

i) Create a Data frame in R for the above project data and display the output.

ii) Show the structure and summary statistics of the Data Frame created.

questions.label: 6b
questions.text: Justify the use of a Content-Based Recommendation System with a specific case study.
